title: Introducing The Forrester Wave™ For Enterprise Firewall Solutions Q4 2026
summary: An evaluation of the 10 enterprise firewall providers that matter most and how they stack up.
body_markdown:
How long does the “next-generation” thing keep that mantle before it’s really just the current generation? What comes after “next-generation”? After nearly two decades you could be forgiven for thinking that firewalls (next-gen and otherwise) have had their time and that, while they may still have one, their place in the security stack is shrinking.


Our latest evaluation of the Enterprise Firewall Solutions market tells a different story. While firewalls may represent fewer distinct points in a network topology, their capabilities are becoming more pervasive throughout the larger network fabric and their control planes are integrating and subsuming functionality from other network security tools and—in some cases—competitors.


As the market has evolved, firewalls have become less and less things that get deployed as singular enforcement points and more and more a set of actions that are taking place throughout the network.


Although proponents of the “big, dumb pipe” model may argue otherwise, the network will continue to play an important role in cybersecurity, and enterprise firewalls will continue to be centerpieces of the security stack because:


- **Defense-in-depth still matters, even with a vanishing perimeter.** Cliches earn that designation for a reason. The phrase “an ounce of prevention is worth a pound of cure” has endured since the 18th century and its origins in a letter about firefighting offer a useful metaphor for the practice of cybersecurity. Whether threats are conventional or emerging, architectures and actions that may seem mundane are the basis for durable defenses. Although the delineation between “trusted” and “untrusted” has moved, changed, and shrunk, the necessity of a boundary between them has not. Enterprise firewalls still form part of that boundary in addition to providing important context that is essential for a Zero Trust architecture.
- **Enterprise firewalls deliver security for technology both old and new.** OT and IoT remain popular targets. AI and quantum security bring new challenges. Firewall features like virtual patching, deep packet inspection, and policy enhancements for protocols like WebSocket and Model-Context Protocol (MCP), cryptographic inventory, and quantum-safe TLS proxying give organizations the tools they need to meet the diverse demands of their long tail and leading-edge technologies.
- **Unified network security policy management and enforcement is becoming a reality.** Although the cloud appears to be the new and permanent home for the control planes of many solutions, vendors are beginning to include data plane enforcement that goes beyond cloud-optimized deployment options. Management of Secure Access Service Edge (SASE) through common object databases and rule structure, as well as the ability to migrate some or all SASE services from vendor POPs to on-premises infrastructure when that topology makes more sense and helps improve policy consistency and performance. Management of DPU-based security functions in modern network gear and AI factory infrastructure is also helping to redefine what “firewall” means.


This vendors in this evaluation have a diverse set of profiles, including platform companies like Check Point, Cisco, Forcepoint, Fortinet, HPE, and Palo Alto Networks; companies focused on the managed service provider market such as SonicWall and WatchGuard Technologies; Sophos (whose firewall offering complements their endpoint security); and Versa Networks whose branch firewall has evolved into an enterprise-ready solution.


Resist the temptation to marginalize firewall solutions in your overall security strategy or relegate them to rudimentary access control duties.
